games.summary: Washington 24, New York 21, and the third-down story we leaned on didn't hold. The pre-game numbers favored the Giants by a little more than a field goal: Washington had been near the bottom of the league at staying on the field, and New York's offense had looked crisper with McCarthy than the full-season numbers said. McCarthy's hip turned out fine, and he did his part, with a career-high yardage night and a 66-yard strike to Isaiah Likely that briefly erased a 17-14 deficit. But Daniels was the better quarterback when it mattered. He threw for three scores, survived two fourth-quarter interceptions (one at the Giants' 2-yard line), and won it with a 32-yard touchdown to Diggs. The Giants closed around a point-and-a-half favorite and lost outright, so the Washington side cashed both ways. The lesson for the file: Daniels' recent cold stretch was a three-game sample, and a short-week division game is where those samples break.

details.scheme: Final: Washington won outright as a short road dog. Daniels beat the third-down profile with three TD passes, including the 32-yard winner to Diggs, despite two fourth-quarter picks; McCarthy's hip held up and his 66-yard TD to Likely put New York up 21-17 in the fourth, but the Giants couldn't hold the lead.

games.why: Line fav -6.5; SEA D vs rookie Mendoza
games.summary: Seattle should win, but it isn't a team to lay a touchdown with. The Seahawks' defense is the best unit in the game, especially on third down, and it gets Fernando Mendoza in his first NFL start behind a Raiders run game that hasn't worked all season. That's the whole case for Seattle, and it's a good one. The problem is the other side of the ball. Drew Lock is cleared to start, and he's been sharp in a small sample, but left tackle Charles Cross and guard Quenton Nelson are both out, so he's playing behind a makeshift line. Leonard Williams is out on defense too. Las Vegas' pass defense is soft enough for Lock and Smith-Njigba to find plays, but sacks and stalled drives behind backup linemen are how a 6.5-point favorite wins by four. Seahawks straight-up; Raiders +6.5 is the slightly better side of the number.

games.why: Line fav -9.5; LAR pass vs very soft ARI pass D, Beck starting
games.summary: The Rams should win this, and the third-down mismatch is as lopsided as anything on the slate. Arizona's offense can't stay on the field on third down, the Rams' defense is the best in the league in that spot, and now it's rookie Carson Beck's first NFL start. He also has two interior line starters out and a receiver room so thin that Trey McBride is effectively the whole passing game. Myles Garrett is expected to play, which makes Beck's afternoon even harder. The reason not to lay the full 9.5 is that the Rams are short-handed too: Puka Nacua and Davante Adams are both on IR, and left guard Steve Avila is out, so Stafford doesn't have the weapons to run up a big score. With the total at 38.5, a 17-6 kind of game is the likeliest outcome. Rams straight-up, and we'd lean Arizona to cover the big number.

games.why: Line fav -3.5; PIT offense is the gap
games.summary: Cincinnati should win at home behind the hottest quarterback in football. Joe Burrow has four straight games with at least four touchdowns, and the Bengals' third-down offense is the best in the league, which is how you beat a solid Pittsburgh defense: sustain drives and finish them. The Steelers' path is the run game. Jaylen Warren and Rico Dowdle face a Bengals run defense that can be pushed around, and Cincinnati's own third-down defense has been a liability, so Pittsburgh can shorten the game and keep Burrow on the sideline. Aaron Rodgers' passing hasn't been good enough to win a shootout, though, and Pat Freiermuth is questionable with an illness. Kyle Dugger's absence thins Cincinnati's secondary, but not enough to flip it. Bengals straight-up. At 3.5 the number is about right; we'd lean Cincinnati to cover, without a strong edge.

games.why: Line fav -4.5; LAC offense worst in the league
games.summary: Baltimore should win this, even with Jacoby Brissett instead of Lamar Jackson. The Chargers' offense has been the worst in the league by EPA, and their protection is a big reason: they give up sacks on more than one in ten dropbacks, now without guard Branson Taylor, and Herbert is playing through a finger injury. Ladd McConkey is questionable with a back injury and Brenen Thompson is doubtful, so the receiving corps is thin too. Baltimore's case is simpler: Derrick Henry, a competent veteran quarterback, and a defense that should win the line of scrimmage, though it's missing safety Jaylinn Hawkins. ESPN's model actually has the Chargers as a slight favorite, but the play-by-play data says the opposite, and a total that crashed to 38.5 says the market expects a slog. Ravens straight-up; at 4.5 in a game this low-scoring, we'd shade toward the Chargers getting points but wouldn't bet it.
